text: Millions of people are searching to me, my X-Men this week, and fans are hyped to see the one who bends metal with magnets.
In the movies, Magneto can even pull the iron right out of someone's blood.
Real magnets can get scary strong. A hospital MRI is over twenty thousand times stronger than Earth's magnetic field.
Bring a metal oxygen tank in that room, and it can rip it out of your hands and fling it into the machine.
Tiny paper clips can fly at it as fast as forty miles an hour.
But your whole body only has about four grams of iron. That's about one small nail.
And it's locked up in your blood in a way magnets barely grab. Even inside an MRI, your blood stays right where it is.
But here's the crazy part. Magnets can still lift you.
Scientists put a live frog inside a magnet about ten times stronger than an MRI, and it floated in midair.
The water in its body pushed back against the magnet, just enough to beat gravity. And the frog was totally fine.
The scientist who floated it won a joke prize for it. Ten years later, he won a real Nobel Prize.
Follow for more of the real science behind your favorite heroes.
